verdict.headline: Vessel struck in Hormuz adds physical risk as HD beats and FOMC Minutes loom Wednesday
verdict.label: Physical supply disruption in Hormuz escalates oil risk; HD earnings beat offsets; 30Y 5.31% entering FOMC Minutes tomorrow
verdict.rationale_short: A vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz Tuesday morning, shifting the oil risk premium from a negotiation-failure premium to a physical-supply-disruption premium with Brent near $91. Home Depot's comparable-sales beat (+1.7% vs +0.9% consensus) is the first positive consumer data point of the retail gauntlet, but CFO McPhail's 'frozen housing market' framing constrains the consumer read-through. FOMC Minutes Wednesday cover three dissenters from the July hold with September hike odds near 30%. The level that changes this read: Brent retracing below $88 on no further physical Hormuz action, and 30Y compressing below 5.25% after the Minutes.

trade_setups.asset: Brent Crude — physical vs. negotiation risk premium
trade_setups.thesis: The vessel strike Tuesday morning converts the Hormuz risk premium from a negotiation-failure premium (quick to compress on diplomatic progress) to a physical-supply-disruption premium (requires demonstrated safe passage to unwind). Brent near $91 currently prices the ceasefire-expired status quo, not ongoing physical interdiction. A second strike within 24h adds a materially different layer.
trade_setups.entry: $91 current; $94–95 is the next technically meaningful resistance if physical escalation continues; $88 is the level where a no-further-action scenario would compress back to.
trade_setups.invalidation: No further Hormuz physical incidents within 48h and back-channel Oman-mediated contact resumes; Brent retraces below $89.

trade_setups.thesis: Three dissenters at the July meeting (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) wanted to hike; nine of 18 FOMC members penciled in a 2026 increase. The Minutes (Aug 19, 2pm ET) reveal whether the dissent was driven by fiscal sustainability and Treasury supply-absorption or by CPI persistence. If fiscal sustainability, the 30Y can extend toward 5.40% even with September hike odds near 30%. If CPI persistence only, five consecutive soft prints temper the move.
trade_setups.entry: 5.28% was the trigger (now breached); 5.40% is the next meaningful level; 5.20–5.25% is retracement support on a dovish read.
trade_setups.invalidation: Minutes reveal isolated, inflation-persistence-only dissent; 30Y retraces below 5.25% by Thursday close.

trade_setups.thesis: RDDT begins its first session as an S&P 500 component from $165.38 — below the $177 post-mechanics threshold. The passive mechanics provided no durable floor; the advertising-durability-in-AI-search question is now the active driver. Two closes below $158 (pre-announcement close) would confirm full reversal of the inclusion pop.
trade_setups.entry: $165 current; $177 = fundamental demand present; $158 = inclusion pop fully reversed.
trade_setups.invalidation: Two consecutive closes above $177 on Aug 18–19 confirm fundamental demand met the passive bid.

bear_case: The vessel strike is the first confirmed physical interdiction in the Strait of Hormuz since the ceasefire expired — a qualitative change in risk character that a negotiation-failure premium alone does not price. If Iran conducts a second physical action within 24 hours, Brent extends above $94, the DXY cannot hold a floor, and the 30Y is already above 5.31% with September hike odds elevated. The HD beat narrows the consumer-deceleration probability but does not eliminate it; TGT and WMT carry the remaining weight of that data set. FOMC Minutes Wednesday are not a neutral event: fiscal-sustainability-driven dissent has no natural cap from soft demand data. If SPX closes below 7,650 before FOMC Minutes land, the base-to-bear scenario ratio shifts decisively.
